sentences.l2: 在城市中心，许多老小区建于上世纪八九十年代，规划之初几乎无人预料到私家车会如此普及，车位配比因此严重不足。
sentences.l1: In the city center, many old residential compounds were built in the 1980s and 1990s, and at the planning stage almost no one anticipated that private cars would become so widespread, so the ratio of parking spaces is seriously insufficient.

sentences.l2: 如今，停车难已成为居民日常生活中最棘手的矛盾之一：傍晚时分，狭窄的通道两侧挤满了车辆，连消防通道也被占道停车一点点蚕食，一旦突发意外，救援车辆便难以通行。
sentences.l1: Today, difficulty parking has become one of the thorniest conflicts in residents' daily lives: in the evening, both sides of the narrow lanes are packed with vehicles, and even the fire lanes are gradually eaten away by illegal parking, so that in an emergency, rescue vehicles can hardly pass.

sentences.l2: 业主们指责物业不作为，物业则声称自身并无执法权，双方各执一词，纠纷经年不断。
sentences.l1: Owners accuse the property management of inaction, while the property management claims it has no law enforcement power itself, the two sides each stick to their own story, and the dispute continues year after year.

sentences.l2: 部分社区尝试错时共享周边商场的车位，或引入车牌识别系统来规范出入，收效尚可；然而更根本的困境在于，公共空间的重新分配必然触及各家利益，如何在公平与效率之间取得平衡，仍有赖于漫长的协商与妥协。
sentences.l1: Some communities have tried staggered-time sharing of parking spaces at nearby shopping malls, or introduced license plate recognition systems to regulate entry and exit, with fairly good results; however, the more fundamental predicament is that the redistribution of public space inevitably touches each household's interests, and how to strike a balance between fairness and efficiency still depends on long negotiation and compromise.
